questions.question: Twelve friends are sitting in two parallel lines. There are 6 people sitting in each row and facing a person of the other row. In row 1, A, B, C, D, E and F are seated and all of them are facing north. In row 2, O, P, Q, R, S and T are seated and all of them are facing south but not necessarily in the same order. C, is third to the right of B. C is not an immediate neighbour to either E or A. P is third to the left of S. Neither P nor S are sitting at the extreme ends of any row. F, faces O, who is second to the right of T, and T is not an immediate neighbour to S. Only two people are sitting between Q and T. A, is not facing R. Which of the following pairs could be sitting at the extreme ends?
questions.solution:
Given:

__
 
• 6 people sitting in each row and facing a person of the other row.
 
• In row 1, A, B, C, D, E and F are seated and all of them are facing north.
 
• In row 2, O, P, Q, R, S and T are seated and all of them are facing south.

 

1) P is third to the left of S. Neither P nor S are sitting at the extreme ends of any row.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cec773b22b7a53c9a1470c4cd102dfdfce56a45d3ea436ca64fc502d7bc2b3c7.png] 

2) F, faces **O, who**__ is second to the right of T, and T is not an immediate neighbour to S.

Here, O is second to the right of T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/67357704f8490f61b3d4b9323ef61b804060a6d06fd9ff247579c6041583a98c.png] 

3) Only two people are sitting between Q and T.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5f2c3252beb843499f29b101dafbfad9611c91534f2e1a365983082930f9571d.png] 

4) C, is third to the right of B. C is not an immediate neighbour to either E or A.

5) A, is not facing R.

Here two cases are possible:

Case 1:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/47075bedcd166482b1b7c2333ff584cf0c31257303c409e49e3b3e2b7b60c08b.png] 

Case 2:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/43021ce3c32d665cc6f718a7fd5730c053f8d2094e6039404a88d546e8d5a0a7.png] 

So from the both cases 'RE' and 'TC or TD' pairs are sitting at the extreme ends but TD pair is not given in any options.

Thus we will take pairs of **"RE' and 'TC".**

Hence, 'RE' and 'TC' pairs are sitting at the extreme ends

questions.question: A number is subtracted from 4 times of it and then, the number obtained is added to its (the resultant’s) next number. If this gives the answer as 91, what was the original number?
questions.solution:
**Let the number is ‘x’**

Given:

**1) A number is subtracted from 4 times of it**

=> 4x – x = 3x

**2) Then, the number obtained is added to its (the resultant’s) next number the answer as 91.**

=> 3x + (3x + 1) = 91

=> 6x = 91 – 1

=> 6x = 90

=> x = 90 / 6

=> x = 15

Hence, **‘15’** was the original number.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

Now, check the options (4):

The number is 15

The number is subtracted from 4 times it and then → (15 × 4) - 15 = 60 - 15 = 45

The number obtained is added to its (the resultant’s) next number → 45 + 46 = 91 (Proved)

Hence, ‘15’ was the original number.

questions.question:
Study the given pattern carefully and select the number that can replace the question mark (?) in it.

 
 

 81
 33
 56
 
 

 3
 6
 4
 
 

 54
 11
 ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Here the pattern followed in **each column** is:

**(1st number ÷ 2ⁿd number) × 2 = 3rd number**

**Column 1:** 81, 3, 54

(1st number ÷ 2ⁿd number) × 2

= (81 ÷ 3) × 2

= 27 × 2

= 54 = 3rd number

**Column 2:** 33, 6, 11

(1st number ÷ 2ⁿd number) × 2

= (33 ÷ 6) × 2

= 5.5 × 2

= 11 = 3rd number

Similarly,

**Column 3: 56, 4, ?**

**(1st number ÷ 2ⁿd number) × 2**

**= (56 ÷ 4) × 2**

**= 14 × 2**

**= 28 = 3rd number**

Hence,** “28” **is correct answer

questions.question: ‘Nephrologist’ is related to ‘Kidney’ in the same way as ‘Cardiologist’ is related to ‘______’
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

‘Nephrologist’ is related to ‘Kidney’ → 'Nephrologist' is a doctor who specializes in treating 'Kidney' diseases.

Similarly,

**‘Cardiologist’ is related to ‘Heart’** →** 'Cardiologist'** is a doctor who **specializes** in treating** 'Heart' diseases.**

Hence, ‘Heart’ is the correct answer.

(The sum of the alphabet positional values) × 3 = Number

COACH is coded as 90

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bcc3a1c563439a1d8b778d13aa53e55242730bf1cbb77be5331dfdb17037d105.png] 

(The sum of the alphabets positional values) × 3 = Number

=> (3 + 15 + 1 + 3 + 8) × 3 = 30 × 3 = 90

And,

POST is coded as 210

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1bb65450fca9edc5ee1e199bb95cdc093a2a95a67947bcb0ed6c13528bd0bd8a.png] 

(The sum of the alphabets positional values) × 3 = Number

=> (16 + 15 + 19 + 20) × 3 = 70 × 3 = 210

Similarly,

**NOISE** → 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f9e7182758f781168cecc5be66a715169c56104b3a0356502acc0bd4f1cf4cc.png] 

**(The sum of the alphabets positional values) × 3 = Number**

**=> (14 + 15 + 9 + 19 + 5) × 3 = 62 × 3 = 186**

Hence, 'NOISE' is coded as "186".
